gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 14?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

These conditions align with the market-implied probabilities favoring 33°C (41%) and 34°C (31%), as historical August climatology in Bavaria rarely exceeds 35°C without stronger advection. Recent model runs have shown little shift in the 48-hour window, reinforcing trader consensus around this narrow range while noting that small changes in boundary-layer moisture or wind could nudge outcomes toward 32°C or 35°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent high-pressure dominance over southern Germany, combined with southerly flow, is driving the current forecast consensus for Munich on August 15. This setup favors clear skies, strong solar insolation, and limited cloud development, supporting peak temperatures of 34–35°C according to BBC and timeanddate.com guidance. Minor ensemble spread—Met Office and timeanddate values near 32–34°C versus BBC’s 35°C—explains the tight market distribution, with 35°C at 69.5% implied probability. Light winds further reduce mixing, enhancing surface warming under stable subsidence. Official German Weather Service measurements the following day will resolve the market, with any last-minute model shifts or unexpected cloud cover as the main variables that could alter outcomes.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the LaGuardia Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/ny/new-york-city/KLGA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts and short-range model consensus indicate a peak temperature of 86°F for New York City on August 14, 2026, modestly above the 83°F climatological normal for mid-August. Partly cloudy skies, light winds, and a moderating Atlantic sea breeze are limiting afternoon heating, keeping readings within the narrow 86-87°F band according to current observations and guidance. This strong alignment across authoritative sources explains the market's near-certain positioning on that outcome. A significant shift in sea breeze timing, unexpected convective cloud development, or rapid model revisions could still push the verified high outside this range before observations finalize.

**Forecast models and official guidance from the Met Office and BBC Weather currently indicate a high near 26–28 °C for London on August 16, with sunny intervals and only a low-to-moderate chance of showers.** After a recent heatwave that produced a provisional UK record of 38.1 °C at Kew Gardens, cooler northerly air is gradually arriving from the north, moderating daytime maxima while keeping conditions largely dry.  

Traders have therefore concentrated the highest implied probabilities on 26 °C (41.5 %) and 27 °C (27.5 %), with 25 °C (18 %) also receiving meaningful support; these outcomes sit squarely within the consensus range of the latest numerical weather predictions and align with climatological expectations for mid-August in southeast England once the heatwave subsides.  

Key upcoming data points include the next Met Office and ECMWF model runs and any afternoon updates from the Met Office, which could refine the precise maximum and shift probabilities if steering patterns or cloud cover change.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current ensemble forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models show genuine uncertainty in Tokyo’s August 16 maximum, with solutions clustered around 29–30 °C and limited spread beyond that range. Subtropical high pressure is expected to maintain hot, humid conditions, yet strengthening onshore flow and possible afternoon sea-breeze convergence introduce cooling potential that could cap the peak near 29 °C. Urban heat-island effects and boundary-layer moisture further modulate outcomes, while historical mid-August climatology places the typical daily maximum at 30–32 °C. Traders are therefore weighting the two leading bins almost equally, reflecting both model consensus near the 30 °C threshold and the narrow margin for error in tomorrow’s final observation.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent JMA seasonal outlooks and global model runs point to a strengthened Pacific High sustaining above-normal warmth across Honshu, positioning Tokyo's August 16 maximum near the long-term average of 30–31°C. Latest short-range guidance from AccuWeather and timeanddate.com indicates a peak around 31°C under partly cloudy skies with possible passing showers, which could cap the daily high by limiting afternoon insolation. Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to 29°C and 30°C because ensemble spreads show modest uncertainty from cloud cover, urban heat-island variability, and any late-day frontal influence, while historical analogs and current steering patterns make excursions above 32°C or below 28°C less likely before the next model update.
